This is often done using central differences between adjacent voxels.
**Edge Detection:** Calculate the magnitude of the gradient $|\nabla f|$.
High magnitudes indicate boundaries between different material classes or structures.
**Noise Suppression:** Apply a threshold or smoothing filter to the gradient magnitude to ignore small-scale noise.
Values below a threshold $\tau$ are treated as zero.
**Style Application:** Modulate the final color or opacity of the sample based on the edge strength.
A common approach is to add a bright highlight or increase opacity specifically at high-gradient locations.
**Compositing:** Composite the enhanced samples along the ray using standard front-to-back or back-to-front alpha blending.
It is distinct from Boundary Enhancement as it likely focuses on transparency to see through objects rather than highlighting boundaries.
Gradient computation adds a constant factor overhead per sample.
Performance depends on the GPU model and the complexity of the gradient calculation.
